mission: InSight (Interior Exploration using Seismic Investigations, Geodesy and Heat Transport)

operational_record.cause_of_end: Thick atmospheric dust coating on solar panels reduced electrical output below transmitter threshold
operational_record.historic_feat: First seismological network listening to the internal heartbeat and mapping the 3D crust, mantle, and liquid core of Mars

science_instruments: SEIS (Seismic Experiment for Interior Structure) - ultra-sensitive French broadband seismometer placed directly on Martian regolith under Wind and Thermal Shield (WTS)
HP3 (Heat Flow and Physical Properties Package) - German self-hammering 'Mole' penetrator
RISE (Rotation and Interior Structure Experiment) - X-band radio Doppler tracking of Martian planetary wobble/nutation
APSS (Auxiliary Payload Sensor Suite) - TWINS wind sensors, barometer, fluxgate magnetometer
Instrument Deployment Arm (IDA) with IDC and ICC cameras

historic_discoveries.details: Detected high-frequency seismic tremors and deep low-frequency tectonic quakes originating primarily from Cerberus Fossae fault grabens, demonstrating active volcanotectonism on modern Mars
historic_discoveries.significance: Proves Mars is geologically alive with active magma reservoirs at depth

historic_discoveries.details: Largest seismic event recorded on another planet, shaking the crust for over 10 hours with surface Rayleigh waves circumnavigating the globe multiple times
historic_discoveries.significance: Provided comprehensive structural illumination of global crustal thickness (30 to 72 km)

historic_discoveries.details: Seismic core-reflected SKS waves measured Mars's metallic liquid core radius at 1,830 ± 40 km, indicating a lower density core enriched in sulfur, carbon, oxygen, and hydrogen
historic_discoveries.significance: Core was liquid during ancient dynamo era, explaining remnant crustal paleomagnetism

historic_discoveries.details: Recorded seismic waves and orbital crater creation from fresh meteoroid impacts at 3,500 km distance (Sept 5 2021 and Dec 24 2021 Amazonis Planitia crater producing boulder-sized ice blocks)
historic_discoveries.significance: First time seismic and acoustic atmospheric shockwaves matched to a fresh crater

astronaut_tactical_note: Elysium Planitia is an ultra-flat, rock-free safety zone ideally suited for heavy-lift cargo landings. However, tectonic faulting at Cerberus Fossae (1,500 km southeast) poses seismic shaking risks. Underground habitats should be seismically isolated.
